t:
(a) 
The boundary maps described in this Act shall be on file and available for public inspection in the office of the Secretary or the Secretary of Agriculture with regard to the National Forest System. In the event of discrepancies between the acreages specified in this Act and those depicted on such maps, the maps shall be controlling, but the boundaries of areas added to the National Park, Wildlife Refuge and National Forest Systems shall, in coastal areas not extend seaward beyond the mean high tide line to include lands owned by the State of Alaska unless the State shall have concurred in such boundary extension and such extension is accomplished under the notice and reporting requirements of this Act.
 
    (b) 
As soon as practicable after enactment of this Act, a map and legal description of each change in land management status effected by this Act, including the National Wilderness Preservation System, shall be published in the Federal Register and filed with the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President of the Senate, and each such description shall have the same force and effect as if included in this Act: 
Provided, however, That correction of clerical and typographical errors in each such legal description and map may be made. Each such map and legal description shall be on file and available for public inspection in the office of the Secretary. Whenever possible boundaries shall follow hydrographic divides or embrace other topographic or natural features. Following reasonable notice in writing to the Congress of his intention to do so the Secretary and the Secretary of Agriculture may make minor adjustments in the boundaries of the areas added to or established by this Act as units of National Park, Wildlife Refuge, Wild and Scenic Rivers, National Wilderness Preservation, and National Forest Systems and as national conservation areas and national recreation areas. For the purposes of this subsection, a minor boundary adjustment shall not increase or decrease the amount of land within any such area by more than 23,000 acres.

 
    (c) 
Only those lands within the boundaries of any conservation system unit which are public lands (as such term is defined in this Act) shall be deemed to be included as a portion of such unit. No lands which, before, on, or after the date of enactment of this Act, are conveyed to the State, to any Native Corporation, or to any private party shall be subject to the regulations applicable solely to public lands within such units. If the State, a Native Corporation, or other owner desires to convey any such lands, the Secretary may acquire such lands in accordance with applicable law (including this Act), and any such lands shall become part of the unit, and be administered accordingly.

fable.w: Most of the section is not participation: maps on file for public inspection, Federal Register publication, and written notice to Congress either stay inside the federal government or merely disclose information. However, subsection (a) bars seaward boundary extensions over State-owned lands unless the State of Alaska has concurred. That makes a non-federal government's agreement a precondition to a federal boundary decision, which is coordination with a state before federal action.
fable.s: unless the State shall have concurred in such boundary extension and such extension is accomplished under the notice and reporting requirements of this Act

opus.w: Before boundaries can be extended seaward onto State-owned coastal lands, the State of Alaska, which is outside the federal government, must agree. That brings the State formally into the federal boundary decision. The tempting reasons for Yes don't work: public inspection of maps is only disclosure, and filings with or notice to Congress stay inside the federal government. The State-agreement requirement alone is enough for Yes.
opus.s: the boundaries of areas added to the National Park, Wildlife Refuge and National Forest Systems shall, in coastal areas not extend seaward beyond the mean high tide line to include lands owned by the State of Alaska unless the State shall have concurred in such boundary extension
opus.b: 1. **Tempting readings that fail:** Several phrases sound procedural but don't count. Making maps "available for public inspection" is only disclosure; the public gets no say in any decision. Filing maps with the Speaker and the President of the Senate, and giving "reasonable notice in writing to the Congress," are notices to Congress, which is inside the federal government. In subsection (c), the Secretary's option to acquire land a State or private owner wants to sell is an ordinary land deal, not participation. **What does count:** Subsection (a) bars extending the boundaries of federal park, refuge or forest areas onto coastal lands owned by the State of Alaska "unless the State shall have concurred." The State is outside the federal government, and it must agree before the boundary decision can take effect. That is coordination with an outside party before a federal action, so the answer is Yes.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the federal government to obtain concurrence from the State of Alaska (an outside entity) before extending boundaries to include state-owned lands. This constitutes coordination with an outside party before making a federal decision. The other provisions regarding public inspection of maps or notice to Congress do not constitute participation as they are either passive disclosures or internal government notifications.
qwen_chat.s: the boundaries of areas added to the National Park, Wildlife Refuge and National Forest Systems shall, in coastal areas not extend seaward beyond the mean high tide line to include lands owned by the State of Alaska unless the State shall have concurred in such boundary extension
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "available for public inspection" constitutes participation because the public can see the maps. However, the definition specifies that participation involves consulting or coordinating with outsiders *before* making a decision, or granting rights to sue/object. Mere access to information after a decision or as a static record is not participation in the decision-making process. Another tempting reading is that the requirement for the State to "concur" in boundary extensions is participation. However, this is a condition for the federal action to proceed (a veto power or consent requirement), which is a form of coordination/consultation with an outside entity (the State) before the federal decision (extending the boundary) is finalized. Wait, let's re-read the definition carefully. "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." The text says boundaries shall not extend... "unless the State shall have concurred". This is a requirement for State concurrence (coordination/consultation) before the federal agency extends the boundary. This fits the definition of coordination with an outside entity (State) before a federal action.

However, let's look closer. Is "concurrence" consultation? The definition says "consult or coordinate". Concurrence is a stronger form of coordination. It involves the State. The State is outside the federal government. So this is a "Yes".

Let's double check if there are other parts. "Available for public inspection" is passive. "Published in the Federal Register" is passive. "Notice... to the Congress" is inside government. "Minor adjustments... Following reasonable notice in writing to the Congress" is inside government.

The key phrase is: "unless the State shall have concurred in such boundary extension". This requires the federal government to get agreement from the State (outside entity) before extending the boundary. This is coordination/consultation.

Let's verify the "No" traps. "Reports to Congress" -> No. "Intra-government" -> No. "Applications" -> No. "Right to sue" -> No.

Is "concurrence" considered participation? The definition says "consult or coordinate". Getting concurrence is a form of coordination. It involves an outside party (State). It happens before the decision (extension) is made. So it is Yes.
